items.text:
Let it be — no voice, no adjustment.

Ravick threw the bone at the cave troll (event 970), which makes him the **fourth** person to independently arrive at bone-plus-hungry-animal. The `throw` verb added last turn worked exactly as designed: it parsed, named the target, returned Futile, and fell through into the room — where `troll-look` caught it and gave him the troll's description. So he got a real, plausible response rather than the empty string Edward got. He is 20/20, armed, winning (troll at ~7 HP), has already taken the second stone out of the wall, and was answered once at the altar when he prayed. He needs nothing from me, and a voice from the air mid-swing would only interrupt a man who is playing this world better than anyone since Edward.

The standing to-do is now four-deep in evidence and belongs to the next turn that can actually write: **the troll room should catch a thrown bone.** The verb exists; only the room is missing.
